'''Lionel Chalmers Jr.''' (born November 10, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who currently works as an assistant coach for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is {{convert|6|ft|0|in|m|abbr=on}} in height and played at the [[point guard]] position.

==Amateur career==
Chalmers played his first three years of high school basketball at Notre Dame-Bishop Gibbons in [[Schenectady, New York]]. He then transferred to [[Albany High School (Albany, New York)|Albany High School]] for his senior year.

Chalmers attended [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier University]], where he played [[college basketball]] for four years as an undergraduate and later as a graduate student. As a senior, he led Xavier to the Elite Eight round of the NCAA Tournament. He was inducted into the Xavier University Athletic Hall of Fame in 2015.<ref>[http://www.goxavier.com/news/2015/10/12/athletics_1012151937.aspx "Xavier Athletics 2015-16 Hall of Fame Class Announced"] Xavier Athletics. Retrieved 2016-01-03.</ref>

==Professional career==
Chalmers was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the second round of the [[2004 NBA draft]] with the 33rd overall pick. He played in 34 games in the 2004–05 season with the Clippers, averaging 3.1 points per game and 1.4 assists per game in 12.0 minutes per game. He was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on August 20, 2005, along with [[Marko Jaric]] in exchange for [[Sam Cassell]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2132990 'Sam I Am' to bring playoff experience to Clippers]</ref> He played for the Timberwolves in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 NBA preseason]], but he was released into free agency before the regular season commenced.

He played in the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek A1 league]] with [[AEK Athens BC]] from November 2005 to February 2006, when he then joined [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]] of the [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|Spanish ACB]].<ref>[http://www.hoopshype.com/players/lionel_chalmers.htm HoopsHype - NBA Players - Lionel Chalmers.<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

He played with the [[Phoenix Suns]]' summer league team during the summer of 2006,<ref>[http://www.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/0703suns0703.html Kerr takes shot today with Hill.<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> but he was not retained by the Suns. He also played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] during the 2006 preseason. After the Hawks waived him before the regular season began, Chalmers signed with [[Dinamo Basket Sassari|Dinamo Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] of the [[LegADue|Italian second division]] in December 2006.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Hoopsworld.com |author=Tracy Graven |title=In Development, December 4–7, 2006 |url=http://www.hoopsworld.com/article_19793.shtml |date=2006-12-07 |accessdate=2007-04-27 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070403062201/http://www.hoopsworld.com/article_19793.shtml |archivedate=2007-04-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In May 2007, he signed with the Spanish ACB club [[Basket Zaragoza 2002|Basket CAI Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Euro Basket - Spanish Basket |publisher=Eurobasket.net |url=http://www.eurobasket.com/esp/esp.asp?NewsNo=2&NewsType=2 |accessdate=2007-06-11 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926222727/http://www.eurobasket.com/esp/esp.asp?NewsNo=2&NewsType=2 |archivedate=2007-09-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 2007, Chalmers moved to the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian first division]] team [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]]. After spending a season in Italy, he signed with the Russian club [[Universitet Yugra Surgut]]. He had a successful season in Surgut, as he was the top scorer of the [[Russian Basketball Super League]] with 21.4 points per game. In the 2009–10 season he played with another Super League club, [[Enisey Krasnoyarsk]]. In July 2010 he signed with [[BC Lokomotiv–Kuban Krasnodar|BC Lokomotiv Kuban]].<ref>[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/07/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-lionel-chalmers.html Lokomotiv Kuban signs Lionel Chalmers to a one-year contract]</ref> In 2012, he joined [[Aliağa Petkim]] of Turkey.<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=TUR&PlayerID=38193 Lionel Chalmers]. Eurobasket</ref> In October 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[BC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lionel Chalmers signs with Levski Sofia|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/bulgaria/64636/lionel-chalmers-signs-with-levski-sofia.html|publisher=Sportando.net|accessdate=4 October 2013}}</ref> With them he won the [[National Basketball League (Bulgaria)|National Basketball League]] of Bulgaria.

In July 2014, he signed with [[Reims Champagne Basket|Chalons-Reims]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lionel CHALMERS signe au CCRB|url=http://www.ccrbasket.com/Article/fiche/id/647|language=French|publisher=ccrbasket.com|accessdate=3 July 2014}}</ref> On January 9, 2015, he parted ways with them.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/148026/lionel-chalmers-chalons-reims-part-ways.html Lionel Chalmers, Chalons-Reims part ways]</ref>

==Coaching career==
Chalmers began his coaching career in 2017 as a video coordinator of the [[Orlando Magic]], becoming an associate coach/player development two years later. On August 8, 2021, he became one of the most important full time assistant coach with the Magic.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-name-assistant-coaches-20210808 Orlando Magic Name Assistant Coaches]</ref>

==Personal==
Lionel's cousin, [[Mario Chalmers]], formerly of the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]], was picked in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He was later traded to the [[Miami Heat]], with whom he won 2 consecutive NBA championships.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_acquire_chalmers080626.html HEAT Acquire Draft Rights To Mario Chalmers]</ref> He also has a wife and 3 children.
